literal: Strength to a person is the wealth of the mind; those who lack that are trees, being different only in being called humans.
translation: A person's true strength is the wealth of their mental energy; those who lack it are like trees, differing only in their human form.
modern: ஒருவருக்கு உண்மையான வலிமை என்பது மன ஊக்கமாகிய செல்வமே ஆகும்; அது இல்லாதவர்கள் மனித வடிவம் பெற்றுள்ளார்கள் என்ற வேறுபாடு மட்டுமே கொண்ட மரங்கள் ஆவர்.
explanation: This couplet defines true strength (uram) not as physical power, but as the wealth of inner drive and mental energy (uḷḷa veṟukkai). The poet compares those who lack this inner motivation to inanimate trees (maram). The only difference (vēṟu) between such passive individuals and trees is their outward human appearance (makkaḷ ātalē). Without the active, conscious energy of resolve, a human body is no better than a motionless wooden trunk.
